## Batch goal

**A profitable resource crossing is closed, the Reed Commons recovers the water gate, the player coalition splits, and Redroot Commons and the Reed Commons make a land-and-labour compact on day 200, and the person who pays for it is a woman of about thirty-four who keeps a stall by the wharf who has been on nothing for two hundred days and names the price before she says yes and asks in advance not to be thanked and is not thanked.**

## The beats, in order

1. **0191, day 194, Saturday — the second chapter of that day.** What the first chapter of the day set in motion, and the night before a meeting-ground is poled. **The store on the upper road is shut on it and about a hundred and forty people have a day they have not had in a hundred and forty-five days, and in a room nine hundred miles away a man is going to be told a figure he did not ask for.**
2. **0192, day 195, Sunday, the fortieth day of the Long Month.** The meeting-ground is poled to the flats at Redroot and the question is put to it. **Nobody may summon it and it has to be poled to where the people are, and about nine people are standing on a flat, and the household is one of them, and the day was chosen by nobody and is the only date in four hundred miles that the raft can be poled to.**
3. **0193 and 0194, day 196, Monday.** What the meeting-ground does with a question it cannot answer, and what a body that floats does when the rule is that every household affected by a change must be heard. **The rule is four hundred years old, has no name on it, and was not built by anybody in this book, and this batch may not name it and may not build a better one.**
4. **0195, day 197, Tuesday.** The salt road closes. **The loss falls on the settlement and not on the Reach, and that is the reason the room agreed, and about four hundred and forty people who are drying salt for a buyer nine hundred miles away cannot be reached by anybody in this volume.**
5. **0196 and 0197, day 198, Wednesday — THE COMPACT'S DAY, and it carries two chapters.** **The trestle count is read out in a room by the man who has been keeping it, and it is one hundred and fifty-eight, and it was one hundred and fourteen on the hearing day and eighty-nine on day 129, and the rule is one a day counted from the fortieth day of this flood and from nothing else, and Adrian is not in that room because he is on no roster and holds nothing and he chose that.** The two chapters of this day are the count and the thing that follows it. **The count is read out in Chapter 0196 and the two halves of that day are 0196 and 0197.**
6. **0198, day 199, Thursday — one chapter on that day.** The ground, the labour, the posting, the salt, and the person who pays. **She names the price before she says yes, in her own words, and asks for it to be entered that she said no for nine years and that this is the yes and that the two are the same person and that she is not a different woman today.**
7. **0199, day 200, Friday, the forty-fifth day of the Long Month — the first of two chapters on that day.** The compact read out in the local language, in daylight, in a room, with a date on it, by a person who is the account of it and who is on no roll, **and the line that is a person is *a person may be found*, and it is not the fifth line of the compact of eleven lines and may not be confused with it.** A girl of seventeen reads the whole of it back twice for the people at the back, from a slate and not from her own.
8. **0200, day 200, Friday — the second chapter of that day, and the last chapter of Volume 04.** **Out on the flats the salt road is standing open and empty, and the racks are drying, and at the store on the upper road a queue is still working on a Friday afternoon, and a man of forty-two is standing at the back of his own queue with his hands in his pockets and no reason to be there and no intention of leaving. Nobody turns him out. And the last image is one thing and not a list.**

| Ch | Day | Weekday | Long Month | Load |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0191 | 194 | Saturday | 39th | the night before |
| 0192 | 195 | Sunday | 40th | the meeting-ground is poled |
| 0193 | 196 | Monday | 41st | what a body that floats does |
| 0194 | 196 | Monday | 41st | |

| 0197 | 198 | Wednesday | 43rd | |
| 0198 | 199 | Thursday | 44th | the posting and the salt |
| 0199 | 200 | Friday | 45th | **the compact is read out** |
| 0200 | 200 | Friday | 45th | **the last image of the volume** |

- **A weekday is a figure and day 1 is a Tuesday. Every weekday above is computed from day 1 and from nothing else.** The anchors a writer may check against: day 49 a Monday, day 100 a Wednesday, day 130 a Friday, day 131 a Saturday, day 154 a Monday, day 174 a Sunday, day 179 a Friday, day 189 a Monday, **day 194 a Saturday, day 195 a Sunday, day 196 a Monday, day 197 a Tuesday, day 198 a Wednesday, day 199 a Thursday, day 200 a Friday.** **No chapter may take a weekday from a neighbouring chapter or from a day map.**
- **Day 194 carries two chapters and one weekday and this batch writes the second of them. Both are on a Saturday. There is no Sunday version of Chapter 0191 and no chapter of this batch may invent one.**
- **The trestle count is day 198 less forty, and it is one hundred and fifty-eight, and the rule is one a day from the fortieth day of this flood and from nothing else, and it was one hundred and fourteen on day 154 and eighty-nine on day 129 and any other figure is arithmetic that has not been done.**
- **The days the thirty-nine men under the near gate have gone unpaid are the day minus eighty-five:** one hundred and nine at Chapter 0191, one hundred and twelve at 0195, one hundred and fourteen at 0198, one hundred and fifteen at 0200.
- **The count of silences is ninety-five at day 191 and it stands there on day 194 because the wall spoke on day 191 and repeated the number before it and the count did not move. The running figure is one addition for each day the wall says nothing, so days 192, 193 and 194 are three additions and the figure is ninety-eight at day 194. The figure is paid for at most once in this batch and not in every chapter, and if the wall speaks in this batch the count does not move on that day.**
- **Date forms. Four, and only four.** *The Nth day of this flood* (1–40). *The Nth day of the new month* (26–90). *The Nth day of the month after this one* (91–155). ***The Nth day of the Long Month* (156–220, the Nth is day − 155).** **No chapter in this batch may use the first, second or third form for its own day.** The only two month names in this world are *March*, which is a day landmark and not a form, and *the Long Month*. **The two most recent months of this flood are all in the fourth form and Chapter 0190 is the thirty-ninth day of the Long Month and Chapter 0200 is the forty-fifth.**
- **No §23 figure changes and no §24 figure changes and no §25 figure changes.** Where this batch establishes something new it goes into a new section in the close phase.

## The two chapters this batch exists for

### Chapter 0196 — day 198, Wednesday, the forty-third day of the Long Month, and it is the first of two chapters on that day

- **The trestle count is read out in a room by the man who has been keeping it, in his own hand, dated, counted from the fortieth day of this flood and from nothing else. It is one hundred and fifty-eight.** It was one hundred and fourteen on the sixty-fourth day of the month after this one and eighty-nine on the thirty-ninth day of the month after this one, and forty-four days separate the hearing from this room and there are forty-four in the difference. **Nobody in that room knows what a day of it means. Nobody in this city can find out. The number is correct and nobody can stop it.**
- **Adrian is not in the room, because he is on no roster and holds nothing, and he chose that, and the finding is that a person who is not findable cannot be checked and a person who is findable is a place a person can be found in, and the man keeping the count is neither.**
- **The plan does not call that number by the name of the woman the letter in the same book is addressed to, and no chapter may.** The letter is one line in the same book and it is the only line in it that is not a number, **it has not been sent, there is no route in this world that a letter can travel, it is in no book and no office knows it exists, and the man keeping the number has still not mentioned it. That is Volume 05's and Volume 10's and it is not resolved here and it may not be softened, and no chapter in this batch may have him mention it.**
- **And the number goes on a wall, in the ordinary course, in a form, and cannot be unmade. A correct page is a page nobody can argue with, and a page nobody can argue with is a page nobody can stop, and the volume that ends with one is a volume that has learned the lesson it has been teaching and still cannot help it.**

### Chapter 0199 and Chapter 0200 — day 200, Friday, the forty-fifth day of the Long Month, the two chapters that close the volume

- **The compact is made on day 200, a Friday, in daylight, in a room, with a date on it, read out in the local language by a woman of about thirty-four who keeps a stall by the wharf, who is on no roll of anything, who has been on nothing for two hundred days and says so first, and whose name goes on a page for the first time in nine years of refusing to be on one.** A girl of seventeen reads the whole of it back twice for the people at the back, from a slate and not from her own, because her own has her name at the top of it. **About nine people in the room and about two hundred and forty who can hear out of a hall, a landing and a market below it, and that is the sixth time about two hundred and forty people have heard something in that room.**
- **Eleven lines of a land-and-labour compact.** The ground stays with the households. No land right of any kind is transferred. No workway is a term of anything and no party to it may be required to surrender one. The labour is shared and posted, and the posting is a page with a date and a price under it, **and a right of refusal that cannot be bought out is on it, because that is the third sentence of the Open Hand, and it cannot be administered, and a man of about thirty-nine who trades on the Open Hand board said so in about nine minutes in the first month of this flood, and he is right, and the compact carries his own objection in it, in his words, dated, because the Commons' own rule is that every household affected by a change must be heard and a man who has been arguing against them for a hundred and ninety days is a household affected by a change.** The salt is a common and not a product. The road is open to everybody on posted days, and the settlement's store is on the same posting and its queue is on the same posting.
- **And the line that is a person is *a person may be found*.** A commons that cannot be found cannot be a party to anything and cannot be answered for, and the finding of this volume is that being findable is the price of being real and not the penalty for it. **Nobody in this volume may be a party to a compact and unfindable, and that is the compact's cost and it is a person.**
- **And that person is the woman of about thirty-four who keeps a stall by the wharf. She takes it. She names the price before she says yes, in her own words, and asks for it to be entered that she said no for nine years and that this is the yes and that the two are the same person and that she is not a different woman today. Nobody thanks her and she asks in advance not to be thanked.** She has been on nothing for two hundred days. She has a slate she has carried for nine years and has never written on and **this batch is not where the slate is explained and it may not be explained here**, and she is on a page for the first time in nine years.
- **And it is not a reconciliation, it is not a speech about a person, and the compact is not the eleventh shape.** The eleventh is a compact of guests whose fifth line is a person who may stop being a guest, and this one's person is a person who may be found, **and a document that can be ended by the asking of a person and a document that requires a person to be findable are not the same instrument and neither is a copy of the other.** The compact of eleven lines is not ended in this volume and the provisional recognition is not ended and no chapter finds the form that would let a district be described as not recognised.
- **And the last image of Chapter 0200 is one thing and not a list.** A man of about forty-two is standing at the back of his own queue with his hands in his pockets and no reason to be there and no intention of leaving, and nobody turns him out, and a compact nobody can check is better than a list anybody can be angry at, and about two hundred and forty people in a market know both of those sentences and neither of them helps.

## The five prose instructions, from `outline/volume-04.md` §17, and what the two batches before this one did with them

1. **A chapter may not open by summarising itself, and least of all its ending. The opening sentence states a pressure or an arrival. It does not state the finding, and the finding is the thing the chapter is for.** **Across forty chapters, three openings were rewritten for this and two of the three stated the finding in the first sentence and one carried a note about what the chapter was about, and a repair pass cut five more craft notes out of the second twenty — *the thing this chapter is for*, *nobody in this book is going to be able to find a more interesting thing to write about*, *here is the whole of it in about four hundred words*, a note about what may not be said again, and a sentence that gave away that the volume ends with a compact.** Do not write a sentence about what a chapter is about, and do not write a sentence that gives the reader the end.
2. **The bolded ledger paragraph may not open a chapter, and a figure that is not load-bearing may not appear in bold at all.** **There is no bolded day-and-weekday ledger paragraph in any of the forty chapters and the licence age, the fee and the palm line are not in any of them.** **All forty of the first twenty were taken out by a review repair pass and this figure is measured on the files as they stand. Do not read it as a claim that the first twenty were clean when they were written; §16 of the Batch 0002 record is the repair record and it is binding.** A figure is paid for once, in a mouth, attached to a decision, and again only when it changes. **The cost column is unchanged and it is recited once across forty chapters; this batch may recite it once and no more, and the trestle count is the only figure in this batch that is new and it is paid for once in a mouth in Chapter 0196 and not again.**
3. **The closing coda is cut by at least half and may not enumerate the standing threads.** One thread, one image, one thing that changed and one thing that did not. **Measured on the last paragraph of each of the forty files as they stand after the Batch 0002 repair pass, the codas run from 12 to 122 words, median about 41, and the construction stands in none of them. The construction to avoid is not the one that was named: it is *And the last thing on the page is…*, and it stood in seventeen of the second twenty chapters renamed rather than removed. A rename is still the formula.** A chapter may end on a figure, a hand, a door, a queue, a rope, a bell, or a sentence somebody said and will not say again, and on nothing else. **Chapter 0200 is the last chapter of the volume and its last image is a man standing at the back of a queue and it may not become a list of the volume's threads.**
4. **The *about N seconds* refrain is used deliberately and sparingly, at most once in a chapter and never twice, and the same limit is set on the two motifs that travel with it — *a person who does not want to be asked*, and *in about nine seconds*.** **Fourteen instances across the second twenty chapters after the repair pass, once each, in fourteen different chapters, against seven across the first twenty and 245 across Volume 03's fifty. The batch was first written with fourteen and six of them were doubled; the six doubles are cut and the count is honest now.** The bare sentence *Nobody said anything for about nineteen seconds* is the one to cut first, and four bare *about four seconds* were cut in the second twenty chapters. **A pause that matters is a thing a person does with their hands.**
5. **The people who carry this volume have a second handle beside the age and the trade and never instead of it** — a name, a habit, a piece of clothing, a thing they do with a pen. **The full list is in `bible/characters.md` §15c and the handles are: Adrian Vale, a name given to him; Hessa Ruun, who counts water on the fingers of her left hand; the keeper of the Redroot gate, a board in her left hand; Nerra Fenn, her hands before her mouth; the woman of about thirty-four who keeps a stall by the wharf, a slate she has carried for nine years and has never written on; Jonah Pike, a printed sheet with a wage on it that he hands over before he says a word, and a blank one; a man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall, a slate he writes on when he is told not to; Bel Dain, a room with a bench in it facing a door; a girl of seventeen, a plain slate and her own with her name at the top of it.** **The device produced two phantoms in the first two batches and both were repairs, and a third is not to be tolerated, and a person invented to hold a line the chapter says was spoken by somebody who is not in the room is the exact failure that has happened twice.**

**And the thing the five exist for: nobody in Volume 03 got stronger and nobody in Volume 04 got stronger. The gains of this volume are a share, a name he did not choose, a month, a date, a gate that came back, and a woman who went on a page on purpose. None of them is a power. One of them is the price of a power. All of them are heavier than a power.**

## The checks, and the two that are cheap

1. **Recompute every weekday from day 1 and grep the ten files for weekday words. Every weekday word inside a chapter that refers to its own day or to a dated day before it is in scope. A check list that says *clean* is a claim about ten files and it is the most expensive sentence in a state layer, because the phase after this one reads it and does not re-run it. Re-run it.**
2. **Subtract.** For every figure in a chapter that has an anchor, do the subtraction from the anchor and not from a neighbouring chapter: the Long Month day number, the days the men have gone unpaid, the days the channel has been shut, the trestle count, the silence count, the days since the day the thing happened. **Nine of Volume 03's nineteen findings were one fault — a figure copied out of a neighbouring chapter instead of computed, in a sentence that reads perfectly. The second twenty chapters of this volume produced six of that fault in their first pass and all six were found by extracting every `N days` phrase with a script and reading it against the day it is measured from. Do it that way and not by eye.**
3. **Check the date forms by grep.** `of this month`, `of the month`, `of the month after this one`, `of the new month`, `of the Long Month`, `of this flood`, and any month form this batch has not established. **No chapter may use the first three forms for its own day, and *the last day of the month before this one* is a form this calendar does not have — one was written in Chapter 0175 and removed.**
4. **Check the *knock* count and the Owen Park count by grep. Both must be zero.**
5. **Check the *about N seconds* count, the coda lengths and the ledger-paragraph count by hand, against the targets above. No chapter may carry more than one of the seconds motif, the *person who does not want to be asked* motif, or the *in about nine seconds* motif.**
6. **Check that no chapter states a finding in its first sentence and that no chapter opens on a note about what the chapter is about, by reading the first two lines of each of the ten.**
7. **Check that every name and every place this batch introduces is established in a room, in daylight, with a date on it, and that none of them is established by narration, and that no person is invented to hold a line the chapter says was spoken by somebody who is not in the room.**
8. **Check the two distances by grep. Nine is the upper road; eleven is the Reach; anything that needs a distance it does not have gets *up the road past this city*.**
9. **Check that no chapter rescues the keeper of the Redroot gate, that no chapter has her say she would say yes again, that no chapter makes her glad, that no chapter argues with her in a room, and that the phrase *the whole of her* is not used about her at all.**
10. **Check the last chapter against §16 of the outline and against `outline/series.md`, and check that nothing in it is improved on by the next volume and that nothing in it is a summary of this one.**

`PHASE_SYSTEM.md` is the standard: **approximately 2,200–3,200 words for an ordinary chapter, longer where a complete scene, a naming or an emotional payoff needs the room.** Counted with `wc -w` on the files as they stand, **Volume 04 Batch 0002 is a minimum of 2,182, a median of 2,298 and a maximum of 3,620, and that is the figure to beat. The three chapters in this batch that may run long are 0196 (the compact's day and the count), 0199 (the compact read out) and 0200 (the last image of the volume).** **Never pad, never split a complete scene to hit a number, never resolve a mystery to get to an ending, and never make a chapter shorter by cutting the thing it was for. Re-count after any repair, not at the end.**

## The rule this run must not break

**A plan is a plan and the pages are not.** The box is shut. The four Elms' fourth channel is shut and a woman of forty-eight in a fourth house is not asked. The sixth reading is not taken and the twenty-fifth is not taken. The delegation has not left and nobody has been asked whether they will go, and the only instruction it has is *to open nothing*, and that clause belongs to the woman of twenty-nine. The eight names at the foot of a hundred-and-forty-year-old page are not read. The room at the far end of the Narrow Mark is unlooked at. The letter in the book on the trestle is one line, it is not a number, it has not been sent, and the man keeping the count has still not mentioned it. **And a chapter that resolves a thing this volume is going to spend four movements on is a chapter that has spent the volume's own material on nothing.**

**And the one sentence that is the volume, and it was said once, in Chapter 0154, at a junction, in the local language, and nobody may improve on it and nobody may say it in narration: a gate is not owned, what a household has is the days on it, and the only way a household loses a gate is by agreeing — and if it gives the days it still has the gate.**
